candidates.heuristic_context: Target problem types: delays caused by batch processing or periodic handling of cases, accumulation of waiting cases before execution. Applicable structural situations: activities executed in batches or triggered periodically instead of being processed immediately when a case arrives. How the data is used: Repeated patterns where multiple cases start the same activity at nearly identical timestamps or where long waiting times precede activity execution indicate batch or periodic processing instead of case-by-case handling. Transformation style: redesign the process so that cases are processed individually upon arrival instead of waiting for batch or periodic execution. Feasibility: Yes. Batch patterns and periodic execution behavior can be detected from event log timestamps, and the process can be redesigned to enable case-by-case execution.
candidates.additional_context: Target was remapped from 'A_Cancelled' (a lifecycle state-change event flagged as batched by pm4py because the underlying work being batched leaves a clustered-timestamp signature there) to 'W_Complete application', the work activity that consistently precedes it within cases. The W_ activity is the real redesign target — the quantitative evidence (batch_size, gap, waiting_time) below remains attributed to the original A_/O_ event, which is where the batching signal is observable. The execution rate meets or exceeds the arrival rate, suggesting that case-by-case processing is feasible without additional capacity. The average batch size is 83.5 cases, which is large. Transitioning to case-by-case processing would significantly change the workload pattern for this activity. This activity exhibits rework in 2 cases (0.0% of all cases). Rework in a batched activity may indicate that batch errors propagate across multiple cases. Whether batch execution can be replaced by case-by-case processing depends on system scheduling policies, operational constraints (e.g. external system availability windows), and whether downstream systems require batched input — none of which can be determined from the event log alone.
